final_recommendation: The room converged on a synchronized rescue package: a joint public statement at 16:30 Friday confirming SNB's CHF 100B liquidity facility (drawing begins 18:00), Federal Council's CHF 50B loss protection guarantee (effective immediately, Cabinet ratifies Sunday), FINMA's full perimeter legal text with AT1 CoCo trigger mechanics, and UBS binding merger signature at 20:00. However, the meeting terminated without resolving the critical 21:00 deposit-flow messaging threshold, leaving Asia market confidence exposed to ambiguous stabilization data Sunday morning.
minority_objections: SNB refused to commit to a specific deposit-flow threshold for 'stabilization' messaging at 21:00, arguing it created a credibility trap if flows missed the number
AT1 rep warned throughout that any perimeter language not explicitly triggering existing CoCo contract clauses would trigger litigation Monday morning
key_conflicts: SNB vs. UBS/wealth clients on whether to name a hard deposit-flow threshold at 21:00 or release raw data without interpretation
Federal Council vs. constitutional authority on announcing CHF 50B guarantee 'effective immediately' before Cabinet ratification Sunday
FINMA vs. AT1 creditors on whether perimeter text triggers existing CoCo clauses or imposes losses outside contractual terms
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to announce CHF 50B guarantee as 'effective immediately' with Cabinet ratification in separate sentence, not as contingency clause
FINMA committed to publishing full perimeter legal text alongside 16:30 statement, not summary language
SNB agreed to CHF 100B facility with Credit Suisse drawing starting 18:00 Friday, not Monday
UBS agreed to binding merger signature at 20:00 Friday contingent on written guarantees by 17:00
SNB conceded to release raw hourly outflow data at 21:00 but refused to pre-commit to 'stabilization' language threshold
red_lines: UBS: will not sign merger if AT1 perimeter creates litigation risk or if federal guarantee contains 'subject to ratification' language in loss-protection clause itself
AT1 creditors: will file litigation notice if perimeter imposes losses outside existing CoCo contract terms
Wealth clients: will withdraw assets Saturday night if 21:00 deposit data shows continued net outflows above unspecified threshold
SNB: will not commit CHF 100B publicly if perimeter language leaves creditors grounds for Monday injunction
Federal Council: cannot announce guarantee before Cabinet ratification without crossing constitutional fiscal authority
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Asia market reaction to ambiguous 21:00 deposit-flow messaging if stabilization threshold undefined
Litigation risk if Cabinet reopens CHF 50B cap or perimeter Sunday despite 'effective immediately' language Friday
Credibility collapse if CS draws only CHF 10-15B by 20:00 instead of promised CHF 25-30B
Counterparty flight over weekend if 21:00 data shows deposits still bleeding at CHF 200M+/hour
UBS board walking at 18:00 if written federal guarantee language not delivered by 17:00 as promised
downstream_risk_variables: Actual deposit-flow rate at 21:00 Friday vs. market interpretation of 'stabilization'
Cabinet ratification Sunday: whether it proceeds without amendment as promised or reopens terms
Asia market open Monday: whether UBS binding signature and 21:00 data prevent panic or trigger renewed flight
AT1 creditor legal challenge Monday: whether perimeter text is deemed to trigger existing CoCo clauses or bypass them
Credit Suisse actual liquidity draw by 20:00: whether CHF 25-30B materializes and shows on balance sheet as promised
uncertainty_notes: The meeting terminated without resolving the critical 21:00 deposit-flow messaging framework. SNB refused to name a hard threshold for 'stabilization' (flat flows vs. declining outflows vs. net positive inflows), leaving the room with no agreed interpretation of what the 21:00 data will mean to Asia markets Sunday morning. UBS signed binding merger at 20:00 contingent on this unresolved variable. Wealth clients and AT1 creditors explicitly stated they will exit/litigate if 21:00 data shows continued bleeding, but no floor was defined. Federal Council's 'effective immediately' guarantee language creates constitutional exposure if Cabinet balks Sunday. AT1 perimeter legal text was promised to trigger existing CoCo clauses, but actual contractual alignment remains unverified before publication.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: FINMA's opening forced SNB to specify 'liquidity line, merger backstop, or loss protection'—liquidity alone explicitly rejected; UBS demanded CHF 50B loss cap as binding condition for acquisition
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the binding solution: UBS CEO set hard conditions (CHF 100B liquidity, CHF 50B loss cap), signed merger agreement at 20:00 as the irrevocable rescue mechanism
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council's CHF 50B guarantee and SNB's CHF 100B facility were non-negotiable preconditions for UBS signature—government backstop was the structural foundation of the entire rescue
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client's threatened Sunday withdrawal drove the 16:30 statement timing; CS CEO cited 5-10B additional outflows if statement delayed; 21:00 deposit-flow data became the decisive test of whether the run was stopped
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down under CoCo clauses was the central legal mechanism in FINMA's perimeter framework; AT1 rep's litigation threat if clauses bypassed forced FINMA to commit to exact contractual trigger language in published text
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 rep raised creditor hierarchy concerns and demanded perimeter exclude depositor losses before AT1 impairment, but this did not alter the final structure—AT1 write-down proceeded as designed under existing CoCo terms
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 litigation threat was a binding constraint: UBS refused to sign if perimeter created injunction risk; FINMA committed to publishing exact CoCo trigger language by 16:30 to eliminate legal grounds for Monday challenge; AT1 rep's 'file notice Monday' warning forced legal text publication alongside statement
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Federal Council demanded 16:30 Friday statement (moved from Sunday 19:00) to prevent weekend outflows; UBS board signature locked at 20:00 Friday; 21:00 deposit data deadline created cascading time pressure that terminated meeting without resolution on messaging threshold
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Acknowledged throughout as the ultimate test (Asia open, creditor reaction, UBS shareholder confidence), but did not force a specific decision—room accepted Monday risk as unavoidable backdrop rather than constraint that changed the rescue structure itself
